```{python}
#| label: setup
import sys
from pathlib import Path
ROOT = Path.cwd()
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

from compare import comparison_table, coefplot, render_table
```

## Balanced vs unbalanced---IDN consumption, urban

The five covariate sets fan across the columns; balanced and unbalanced versions are grouped under the column spanners.
Stars: <sup>\*</sup> p<0.10, <sup>\*\*</sup> p<0.05, <sup>\*\*\*</sup> p<0.01.
Standard errors in parentheses.

```{python}
#| label: idn-bal-vs-unb-table
#| output: asis
fix    = {"country": "IDN", "depvar": "consumption", "choice": "urban"}
versus = {"unbalanced": "cuu", "balanced": "cub"}

table = comparison_table(fix=fix, versus=versus)
print("```{=html}")
print(render_table(table))
print("```")
```

```{python}
#| label: idn-bal-vs-unb-coefplot
#| fig-cap: "Point estimates with 95% CI by covariate set, balanced and unbalanced offset within each row."
#| out-width: "100%"
coefplot(fix=fix, versus=versus);
```

## Balanced vs unbalanced---CHN consumption, urban

Same comparison for China.
Hansen's $J$-test is known to reject in the pooled CHN sample; splitting by hukou status is the documented fix and is not yet wired into this view.

```{python}
#| label: chn-bal-vs-unb-table
#| output: asis
fix    = {"country": "CHN", "depvar": "consumption", "choice": "urban"}
versus = {"unbalanced": "cuu", "balanced": "cub"}

table = comparison_table(fix=fix, versus=versus)
print("```{=html}")
print(render_table(table))
print("```")
```

```{python}
#| label: chn-bal-vs-unb-coefplot
#| fig-cap: "Point estimates with 95% CI by covariate set, balanced and unbalanced offset within each row."
#| out-width: "100%"
coefplot(fix=fix, versus=versus);
```

## Main vs experience-extras---IDN consumption, urban (unbalanced)

The "main" side fans across the standard five covariate sets.
The "experience" side runs the GMM with `exp` (years of work experience) added as an extra regressor in every column, so its ladder is c1 (extra+period FE) through ca (extra+female+age$^2$+edu).
Different cov-set lengths sit side-by-side: 5 columns for main, 4 for experience.

```{python}
#| label: idn-main-vs-exp-table
#| output: asis
fix    = {"country": "IDN", "depvar": "consumption", "choice": "urban", "balance": "unbalanced"}
versus = {"main": {}, "experience": {"family": "exp"}}

table = comparison_table(fix=fix, versus=versus)
print("```{=html}")
print(render_table(table))
print("```")
```

```{python}
#| label: idn-main-vs-exp-coefplot
#| fig-cap: "Point estimates with 95% CI. Cov-set rows on the y-axis use the main convention; experience markers appear only on rows it has."
#| out-width: "100%"
coefplot(fix=fix, versus=versus);
```

## Pooled vs rural-first hukou---CHN consumption, urban (unbalanced)

CHN sample split by hukou regime.
"pooled" is the headline CHN spec; "rural-first" restricts to individuals whose initial recorded hukou is rural.
The hukou-split sters share the same five-covariate ladder as the main fits, so the columns line up one-for-one.

```{python}
#| label: chn-pooled-vs-rf-table
#| output: asis
fix    = {"country": "CHN", "depvar": "consumption", "choice": "urban", "balance": "unbalanced"}
versus = {"pooled": {}, "rural-first": {"hukou": "rf"}}

table = comparison_table(fix=fix, versus=versus)
print("```{=html}")
print(render_table(table))
print("```")
```

```{python}
#| label: chn-pooled-vs-rf-coefplot
#| fig-cap: "Point estimates with 95% CI. Hansen's $J$-test should sit in a more reasonable range under the rural-first split."
#| out-width: "100%"
coefplot(fix=fix, versus=versus);
```
